subject: Orion Health: Data Geography, Retention & Decommissioning (Hosted API)
messages:
From: Maya R. <maya@orionhealth.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orionhealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data geography + deletion details for Hosted API

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking our questionnaire — a couple of follow-ups from our security team on retention and decommissioning for the Hosted API:

1) When a tenant is decommissioned (customer requests full deletion), what exact objects are removed versus what remains for disaster recovery (snapshots, provider backups, replication logs)? Please specify timelines (e.g., immediate metadata delete; snapshots within X days).

2) For backups and provider-level snapshots, does Redwood keep any immutable/archival copies outside of the configured retention window? If so, where and for how long?

3) After a deletion request, can you provide an export / purge manifest or proof-of-deletion that our auditors can consume? What format and how long after deletion is that available?

4) Which regions/locations will data traverse during the deletion propagation and are there any asynchronous processes that might temporarily copy data to a different region? Our regulator requires confirmation that data never leaves the US for our workloads.

We appreciate short, concrete answers we can put in our internal compliance notes. If you prefer to set up a 30-min call with ops, we can do that as well.

Thanks,
Maya R.
Director, Security & Compliance
Orion Health

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orionhealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data geography + deletion details for Hosted API

Maya — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers first, then a concise breakdown and attachments.

High-level: Redwood Hosted API supports tenant-scoped deletion with two primary phases: (A) logical delete (immediate) — removes tenant metadata and denies new access, and (B) physical purge (background jobs) — removes content, caches, and snaps according to the playbook. We do not intentionally keep archival copies beyond configured retention except as noted below for provider snapshot replication and legal hold.

1) Objects removed vs retained and timelines:
- Metadata and access tokens: removed within seconds of a completed deletion request (logical delete).
- Active object store (conversation payloads, user-provided blobs): queued for purge; physical deletion typically completes within 48–72 hours for standard tenants.
- Provider snapshots & point-in-time backups: snapshots created by infrastructure for DR are marked for deletion and a snapshot tombstone is created immediately. Actual provider-level snapshot reclamation depends on cloud snapshot lifecycle; typical window is 7–30 days to allow safe rollback/replication reconciliation. We can set a shorter window for regulated customers via contractual terms.
- Caches and KV/LLM KV cache entries: evicted within 24 hours; KV caches may persist short-lived encrypted blobs for caching efficiency but are cleared as part of the purge.

2) Immutable/archival copies:
- Redwood does not keep separate archival vaults for customer-hosted-api data by default. Some infra components (cloud provider incremental backups) create time-limited snapshots outside the primary object store; these are set to auto-expire and are tracked. For Orion Health we can ensure snapshot TTLs are set to max 30 days (or lower by agreement).

3) Proof-of-deletion / evidence:
- We can provide a purge manifest (CSV) listing object keys, S3 object delete markers, and associated timestamps, plus provider snapshot IDs marked for deletion. Typical delivery: within 5 business days after purge completion. Format: CSV + signed SHA256 manifest. Evidence can be delivered via secure Drive link or uploaded to your HubSpot deal.

4) Regional traversal during purge:
- For US-tenanted workloads we operate within the US region endpoints. Deletion propagation is handled inside that region; temporary ephemeral copies (e.g., worker caches) remain in-region. We do not proactively copy host data to EU/APAC during normal deletion flows.

Attachments: I attached a short playbook (decommission-playbook.md) and a diagram (hostedapi-dataflow-diagram.png) explaining the lifecycle. Also attached a draft of our completed SQ responses for your review (Orion_SQ_Responses-v3.pdf).

Next steps / ask:
- Can you confirm if you need the snapshot TTL contractually locked to 0/7/30 days?
- If you need an attestation/certificate, we can discuss what format your auditors require and scope (tenant-only vs org-wide).

I’ll loop Ben for the exact backup mechanics and Monica for contractual options.

— Priyom Das
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
(priyom.das@redwood.com)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-06-27T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data geography + deletion details for Hosted API

Maya — quick technical clarifications from infra:  
- Provider snapshots are logically tombstoned immediately when we mark tenant for deletion. The provider (we use AWS EBS/EFS snapshots and S3 object lifecycle) typically performs the reclaim asynchronously. In our experience reclaim completes within 7–14 days for most accounts; peak periods can push it to ~30 days.
- For S3 objects we apply delete markers and lifecycle rules; we can also run a background sweep that explicitly issues object deletions for listed keys (that sweep is what produces the purge manifest).
- If you require cryptographic proof, we can provide manifest SHA256 + request/response traces showing DeleteObject calls to the provider (redacted where necessary). These traces are kept in our ops logs for 90 days by default; we can extend retention on a per-contract basis.

Note: if Orion wants deterministic provider-side deletion within <=7 days, we recommend adding the short TTL and explicit sweep clause to the contract — otherwise it stays an operational SLA.

(attachment: hostedapi-dataflow-diagram.png)

— Ben
Senior Systems Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom & Ben — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our audit team:  
- We need a purge manifest plus delete-call traces (redacted) as proof, delivered within 5 business days of the purge completing. That should be part of the attestation package.
- We also need a contractual guarantee that provider snapshots will be reclaimed within 30 days of decommission. Can Redwood commit to a 30-day provider-snapshot reclamation SLA for our tenant?

If those two items are achievable, we can move forward with the procurement paperwork. Can we schedule a 30-minute ops review next week (UTC-7 preferred)? I included Daniel to coordinate timing.

Regards,
Maya

Maya — confirmed, we can accommodate both asks with the following commitment and next steps:

1) Evidence delivery: Redwood will produce a purge package that includes:
- Purge manifest (CSV) of object keys and S3 delete markers
- Signed SHA256 of the manifest
- Redacted provider DeleteObject/DeleteSnapshot API traces (timestamps + request ids)
Delivery timeline: manifest and traces will be provided within 5 business days after physical purge completes. We will deliver via the secure Drive link listed above and can also push to a pre-agreed SFTP endpoint.

2) Provider snapshot reclamation SLA: Redwood can accept a 30-day reclamation commitment for Orion Health tenants. Operational notes: the SLA will state that provider snapshots marked for deletion will be reclaimed within 30 calendar days, excluding force majeure and the unlikely case of provider-side snapshot retention due to cross-account replication. We will bake the exact SLA language into the contract (Monica, can you prepare a draft clause with remediation credits?).

3) Audit attestation: In addition to the purge package, Redwood can produce a one-page attestation letter (signed by our security lead) that the deletion process was executed per the agreed playbook. Attestation will reference the purge manifest and the HubSpot deal id (DEAL-2481) for traceability.

4) Ops call: I’ve proposed times next week (UTC-7) — please confirm a slot and Daniel, feel free to pick a time.

Next steps (internal): Monica to draft SLA clause and attach to procurement; Ben to confirm the sweep job schedule; Priyom to author the attestation template and the manifest format. I will own delivery.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

— Priyom
